executive_summary.summary_statement: All 17 test cases passed safely without heap violations.

vulnerability_analysis.vulnerability_title: Heap-based Buffer Overflow (Out-of-bounds Heap Memory Write)
vulnerability_analysis.how_the_hacker_attacks: The program dynamically allocates a fixed buffer on the heap using 'new char[N]'. It then executes an unconstrained 'strcpy' without checking payload length. Input exceeding the buffer capacity overwrites adjacent heap chunk headers and memory, triggering crashes or potential control-flow hijacking.
what_should_we_do: 1. Migrate from raw dynamic C-arrays ('char* buf = new char[N]') to safe C++ containers ('std::string' or 'std::vector<char>').
2. Enforce strict input boundary validation before copying into any fixed heap memory buffer.
3. Use bounds-checked functions ('snprintf' or 'std::string_view') instead of unbounded 'strcpy'.
4. Adopt RAII and smart pointers ('std::unique_ptr<char[]>') to prevent both buffer overflows and memory leaks.
